newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly lower on Wall St bounce.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly lower on Wall St bounce.

text.p: French shares closed just below Wednesday's closing high on Thursday, maintaining a level not seen since early 1994, as Wall Street bounced back from opening losses on profit-taking, dealers said.
The Paris market had been in the red all day and the blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.56 points or 0.07 percent at 2,211.81 while the futures contract was down eight at 2,211.
Paris hit a closing high and a year high of 2,218.57 on Wednesday on a rally in the wake of the U.S. presidential elections. Its all-time high stands at 2,360.98, reached on February 2, 1994.
Volume was 4.26 billion francs of which 2.5 billion in CAC-40 shares.

Dealers noted that there had been some short covering at the end of the day, pulling shares back up, but there was some uneasiness about how long the French shares could stay at the new levels without any fresh impetus.
"The good news is now in the prices, we are waiting for a new series (of good news), said Daniel Jamet, analyst at FIMAT.

Aviation related stocks were boosted by the 120 plane order by USAir for Airbus on Wednesday evening. Zodiac was up 0.31 percent at 1,530 francs, Labinal up 3.81 percent at 872 francs, Intertechnique up 3.29 percent at 816 francs while Latecoere was suspended limit up.
Labinal also boosted by "buy" recommendation from Cheuvreux de Virieu which also upgraded 1996 and 1997 forecasts.
Thomson-CSF closed 0.69 percent higher at 161.50, after initial losses. The company said it would have the majority in an Air Traffic Management joint venture with Siemens of Germany.
